svg.aria-label: How to write ж: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ж
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ж (cyrillic), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase ж demonstration, 03:16–03:21, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source note on variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 03:16–03:21 lowercase ж demonstration, the pen begins at the lower left, rises through the left arch into the tall central loop, descends through the middle, continues into the right arch, and finishes through a smaller rightward exit without lifting, for one continuous pen-down run and zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a rounded, looped form whose side wings resemble joined cursive arches; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a symmetric printed form with one straight central upright and four diagonal arms. This learner path preserves the source's lower-left-to-centre-to-right order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: rise from the lower-left arm to the central upright, retrace the upright, sweep through the upper-right arm, return to the centre, and descend along the lower-right arm without lifting. Connected cursive may add entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant the wings and central loop differently.
